question: True or false: Americans born around 1860 grew up shorter on average than those born around 1830, though incomes had risen?
answer: True. Military records show average height of native-born American men falling by a couple of centimetres across those cohorts, while income per head grew. John Komlos points to what income leaves out: dearer food as farm goods went to distant markets, and crowded towns full of infection. City children paid in stature.
move: When two measures of welfare part ways, look for what drives both.
trap: Taking rising income per head as a measure of how well people lived.
reference: Komlos, Shrinking in a Growing Economy? The Mystery of Physical Stature during the Industrial Revolution, Journal of Economic History, 1998
